Adjoint gradients for nonlinear and time-dependent problems

Source: R/adjoint.R
nonlinear_sensitivity.Rd

nonlinear_sensitivity() returns the gradient of J(u(theta)) for a nonlinear_problem() family. At the converged state the discrete residual satisfies F(u, theta) = 0; one solve with the transposed Newton Jacobian, J_F^T lambda = dJ/du, gives dJ/dtheta = dJ/du_d du_d/dtheta - lambda' dF/dtheta, where the parameter derivative of the residual is a central difference at the fixed state (no extra nonlinear solves).

Usage

nonlinear_sensitivity(problem_fun, theta, objective, h = 1e-06, ...)

transient_sensitivity(
  problem_fun,
  theta,
  objective,
  dt,
  method = c("backward-euler", "crank-nicolson"),
  h = 1e-06,
  ...
)

Arguments

problem_fun

function(theta) returning a nonlinear_problem() or parabolic_problem().

theta

Parameter vector.

objective

function(u) of the full degree-of-freedom vector (the final state for transient problems) returning list(value = , gradient = ), for example from misfit_objective().

h

Relative difference step for parameter derivatives.

...

Passed to solve_pde().

dt, method

Time step and scheme for transient problems.

Value

A list with value, gradient, the solution and the adjoint.

Details

transient_sensitivity() returns the gradient of an objective of the final state of a parabolic_problem() family solved by backward Euler or Crank-Nicolson (without startup steps). The forward run stores the states; a backward sweep with the transposed step matrix computes the discrete adjoint, and the gradient collects the derivatives of the operator, the loads and the initial condition. It is the exact gradient of the discrete time-stepping scheme (up to the difference steps of the operator derivatives), at the cost of one extra solve per step, independent of the number of parameters. Coefficients must not depend on time and the Dirichlet data must not depend on theta.

Check either gradient with Taylor remainders, as in taylor_test().

Examples

mesh <- pde_mesh_rectangle(nx = 6)
pf <- function(th) nonlinear_problem(mesh, diffusion = function(u) th[1] + u^2, source = th[2],
                                     bcs = dirichlet_bc(0))
ob <- misfit_objective(fe_space(mesh), pde_observations(0.5, 0.5, 0.05))
nonlinear_sensitivity(pf, c(1, 1), ob)$gradient
#> [1] -0.001576247  0.001578797
